minutes.headline: Library trustees approved a one-time contract bridge payment for the director and removed a challenged children's book.
minutes.summary: The Library Board reviewed the FY22 budget and the FY23 request, then voted a one-time payment to cover the director's raise from January to the new July contract start. The director described how a challenged children's book was withdrawn without a board hearing, and trustees discussed precedent. They also reviewed the trustee handbook, bylaws drafting, the town caucus and a food truck idea for Fridays.

budget_items.what_was_said: Seven months in, salaries are on schedule and other expenses are catching up. Heating is running low, but large invoices were recently submitted.

The library asked for a corrected director salary, two new library assistant positions to open Fridays, and increases to heating and electricity. It also asked for more in programs, the full CW MARS membership assessment, library materials and technology.
The fee is rising over a three-year transition to full membership, and this is the second year. The assessment also includes usage, fiber connection and e-rate discounts.
The state requires spending a set share of the municipal appropriation on library materials, so the materials and book service lines were increased.

Money is requested to cover routine replacement and urgent needs, notably the phone system, server and public computers. A trustee said the request would need more detail because it would cover only one of those.
A trustee noted that adding a business day usually raises utilities more. The director derived the figure from the increase in open hours, and a better method was offered to discuss later.
A one-time payment bridges the raise from January 1 to the July 1 start of the fiscal-year contract. It was calculated from paid days in each half-year.

decisions.decision: The challenged children's book was withdrawn from the collection by the director and selector without going to the board.
Policy subcommittee members (Dick, Maya, Kate and Bob named) will review the sample bylaws on their own and then meet in person at the library.
Dick will attend the March 14 town caucus and nominate the two trustees whose terms are up.
The director will look into food trucks for the new Friday openings.

what_happened.line: Library trustees voted unanimously, per the chair, to make a one-time payment to the director to cover the gap before his new contract starts July 1.
The director said a challenged children's book was withdrawn from the collection by him and the selector without going to the board.
Trustees reviewed the FY23 request, which includes a corrected director salary, two new assistant positions to open Fridays, and higher heating, electricity, materials and technology lines.
The CW MARS membership fee is rising in the second year of a three-year move to full membership, and a trustee said the technology request needs more detail.
The policy subcommittee will review sample bylaws and meet in person, and Dick will nominate the two trustees whose terms are up at the March 14 town caucus.

why_it_matters: The FY23 library request, with new staff for Friday hours and larger fixed costs, is the kind of item that reaches the town budget and Town Meeting votes.
A challenged book was removed without a board hearing, so residents may want to know how the library's collection policy handles challenges.
watch_next: March 14 town caucus, where two trustee seats with expiring terms are to be nominated.
The policy subcommittee's review of the sample bylaws, followed by an in-person meeting at the library.
